title: Sanger Tree of Life RNA Extraction: Manual TRIzol™
author: Raquel Juliana Vionette do Amaral

steps.title: Prepare Samples
steps.instruction: Place the samples on dry ice.

steps.title: Homogenize Samples
steps.instruction: Perform homogenization based on sample preparation type.

substeps.instruction: For cryoprepped samples: Label 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes, add 500 μL TRIzol to each, add 500 μL TRIzol to the tube containing the sample, gently mix with a wide-bore tip, and transfer the homogenised sample to the corresponding 1.5 mL tube.

For powermashed samples: Label 1.5 mL BioMasher tubes, add 50–100 mg tissue and 250 μL TRIzol, disrupt tissue using a sterile BioMasher pestle in a Diagnocine PowerMasher II until no large pieces remain, discard the pestle, and add 750 μL TRIzol to the tube.

steps.title: Initial Mixing and Clearing
steps.instruction: Vortex samples for 1–2 seconds on maximum setting.

substeps.instruction: If large pieces of debris remain: Centrifuge at 12,000 × g at 4 °C for 5 minutes and transfer the supernatant to a new, labelled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Lysis Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the RNA from proteins and DNA using chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 μL chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol used for lysis and securely cap the tube.
Incubate for 2 to 3 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g at 4 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Recover Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the RNA-containing aqueous phase to new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.

substeps.instruction: Hold tubes at 45° during removal to avoid aspirating the interphase or red organic phase.
Leave behind a small amount of the aqueous phase if necessary to avoid contamination.
Dispose of the organic phase and interphase unless required for another protocol.
Add 500 μL isopropanol per 1 mL of TRIzol used for lysis.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 20 °C.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g at 4 °C for 10 minutes to form a white, gel-like pellet.

steps.title: RNA Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet with ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the RNA in 1 mL of freshly-made 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol used.
Discard the supernatant, ensuring the pellet does not dry.
Centrifuge at 7,500 × g at 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: RNA Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the RNA pellet in 50 μL of RNase-free water and gently pipette to mix.

steps.title: Thermal Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples at 55–60 °C for 10 to 15 minutes.

steps.title: DNA Removal
steps.instruction: Remove DNA using Turbo DNase treatment following manufacturer instructions.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.1 volume 10X TURBO DNase™ Buffer and 1 μL of TURBO DNase enzyme to the RNA and mix gently.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20–30 minutes.
Resuspend DNase Inactivation Reagent by flicking or vortexing, then add 5 μL to the sample and mix well.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature (use a heat block or oven if room temperature is below 22–26 °C), flicking the tube 2–3 times.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 1.5 minutes and carefully transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Quality Control and Storage
steps.instruction: Verify RNA concentration and quality with required QC and store samples at –80 °C.
